title: The Lore pane gate opens whenever a process is interactive and CLAUDECODE is unset, so an unlabelled process still auto-starts the pane and its 30 s clock
description: The gate at hooks/register.tsx:1271 reads: gated = !e.isInteractive || (await $.env.get("CLAUDECODE")) === "1". A process opens the pane only when it is interactive AND does not carry CLAUDECODE=1. Any interactive process whose environment lacks that variable -- a harness-spawned child, an SDK or dynamic-workflow process that reports interactive, or a launcher that drops the variable -- falls through the gate, auto-opens the pane and registers the 30 s clock, which runs two lore reads per tick and builds .lore/cache in whatever checkout it sits in. FOUND during the LCLI-718 producer measurement (2026-11-18): four isolation-worktree caches were produced by the pane at plugin <= 0.13.x, and this condition is what decides whether the gate stops that on a current plugin. DEC-281 (a3) makes a stray cache harmless for deletion, but the clock is also the host-load risk the LCLI-705 comment records (2026-10-12, load ~300). NOT part of LCLI-718: this is a hook path, so it waits for a plan approval.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The set of processes for which the gate evaluates false is enumerated exactly (isInteractive true AND CLAUDECODE unset), with the harness entrypoints that can produce them named.
A measurement states whether any such process exists in this fleet today, or that none does; naming which entrypoints were probed.
The gate is re-expressed so a person terminal is a positive test, not the absence of two negatives.
Both ways: a gated process opens no pane and registers no clock, and the intended terminal still opens the pane or the chosen replacement is recorded.
